Describe and declare a group dimension

Source: R/group.R
group.Rd

The group() function describes a single group dimension, including valid categories, whether to track ancestry, and inheritance rules. The set_groups() function declares all group dimensions for a hammel_model.

For the set_groups function, each named argument should identify a group name and provide the returned value from a group() function. See examples for syntax.

Usage

group(categories = NULL, ancestry = FALSE, inheritance = group_inheritance())

set_groups(model, ...)

Arguments

categories

Optional complete, ordered vector of the dimension's categories (character labels or finite numeric codes). NULL (the default) either keeps the categories the population already declares, if any, or they are inferred from the population's values in first-occurrence order, plus transition destinations and categories with ancestry shares. When given, every value in the population and every transition destination must be listed; categories can be declared even if starting population contains no members of that category.

ancestry

Logical, default FALSE. Track ancestry shares for this dimension in the simulation output. The returned population then has an ancestry table indicating the share of ancestry from each category of the group. Required for use of the ancestry inheritance method.

inheritance

Either a single character string, a group_inheritance() object, or a calendar schedule tibble with time_start, time_end and a list-column model providing the group inheritance model for a time period. Determines how group membership is assigned to newborns. Defaults to random_parent. Character sting entries will use built-in methods provided gy the group_inheritance model.

model

A hammel_model, used by set_groups().

...

Named group() objects, one per dimension, named by the persons column. No arguments removes the declaration.

Value

group() returns a hammel_group object describing one dimension. set_groups() returns an updated hammel_model.

See also

hammel_population(), generate_uniform_population(), group_inheritance(), group_transition()

Examples

# create two groups - ethnicity and education
model <- hammel_model() |>
  set_groups(
    ethnicity = group(
      categories = c("W", "B", "O"),
      ancestry = TRUE,
      inheritance = group_inheritance("ancestry")
    ),
    education = group(
      categories = c("LHS", "HS", "SC", "C"),
      ancestry = FALSE,
      inheritance = group_inheritance("fixed", fixed_value = "LHS")
    )
  )
